title: Chrome DevTools MCP Server
summary: Let your coding agent open Chrome, read the console and network panel, and record performance traces to debug a live page with DevTools.
description: The Chrome team publishes this server so an agent can use DevTools instead of guessing. It can navigate a page, take screenshots, read console and network activity, and run performance traces to find slow loads.
It starts through npx and needs no account. Chrome must be installed; the server launches its own browser, and a headless or isolated mode is available through flags.
The server sends usage statistics to Google by default and may look up field data for traced URLs. This config turns both off with --no-usage-statistics and --no-performance-crux.
useWhen: Find out why a page loads slowly
Read a console error that only appears in the browser
Check which network request returned a failure
Verify a layout fix after you change the CSS

mcp.name: chrome-devtools
access: Controls a Chrome browser on your machine and can open any URL
Exposes page content, console output and network data to the agent

example.prompt: Open http://localhost:5173, record a performance trace of the load and tell me what delays the largest paint.
example.result: The largest paint is a hero image that starts loading only after a render-blocking script finishes. Preloading the image and deferring the script should move it earlier.

faq.question: Does it send data to Google?
faq.answer: By default it collects usage statistics, and performance tools may query Google's CrUX service. The two flags in this config switch those off.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with pages that hold personal data?
faq.answer: The server hands browser content to your agent, so avoid pointing it at pages with sensitive or personal information, or use the --isolated flag for a throwaway profile.

faq.question: Can I run it without a window?
faq.answer: Yes. Add --headless to the args, or --slim for a smaller tool set aimed at basic browser tasks.

access: Launches and controls Chrome on your machine
